question: Why was 1 of 33 mirror repositories indexed on glama.ai/mcp/servers and 32 not, and what can be done about it autonomously?
headline: Nothing in the repositories discriminates. 24 comparable fields are identical or non-discriminating between the indexed repo and the unindexed ones.

Glama's own methodology page documents NO crawler for open-source servers: listing requires a GitHub OAuth submission from a maintainer with write access. Our record exists anyway, unclaimed, so an unadvertised low-rate ingestion path exists and is not steerable.
The lag from repo creation to Glama record is 33 minutes for one repo and about 120 days for the other repo this account has listed. That spread is a queue, not a filter.

The official MCP registry is the one public no-account signal that demonstrably reaches Glama. It lands at /mcp/connectors, not /mcp/servers, and it is already working: 4 connectors on 2026-09-07 became at least 25 on 2026-09-09 with no action taken.
Connectors carry the identical TDQS rubric and are re-scored about daily, so the tool-description work IS measurable now on 25 servers.
license_activate is the minimum-scoring tool on 20 of 20 connectors. 40 percent of the definition-quality score is the minimum tool score, so one shared description caps the entire fleet.

discrimination.method: Compared the indexed repo (mcp-statement-of-account) against the unindexed ones across every field Glama could plausibly read.

fields.field: Dockerfile builds in its own repo

fields.indexed: same scaffold: src, test, vendor, server.json, smithery.yaml, llms-install.md, remotes.json, SPEC.md

fields.note: glama.ai is a referrer on NONE of them, including the indexed one

fields.discriminates: this is the outcome, not a cause

hypotheses.claim: Crawl-queue position. An unadvertised, low-rate ingestion has simply not reached the other 32.
for: glama.ai/mcp/methodology 1.1 documents open-source listing as GitHub-OAuth submission only, with no crawler. Our record exists unclaimed with an 'Author not verified' checklist item and a Claim flow, so an undocumented path exists.

Creation-to-record lag is 33 minutes for mcp-statement-of-account (created 2026-09-05T17:10:18Z, Glama record 2026-09-05T17:43:09.930064Z) and about 120 days for bln-mcp-grammar-server (created 2026-05-03T05:45:00Z, Glama record 2026-08-31T04:35:21.787402Z). A filter does not produce that spread.
against: n=2 listed records. Not provable from outside Glama.
hypotheses.action: None autonomously. Do not delete and recreate repos to bait a crawler.

hypotheses.claim: Duplicate-source collapse. All 33 mirrors declare repository.url = github.com/theluckystrike/mcp-servers, so a pipeline that canonicalises on the declared upstream keeps exactly one record.
for: Predicts exactly one survivor, which is what is observed.
package.json and server.json both declare the monorepo on all 33.
against: The survivor should then be the first seen (mcp-time-tracker, created 2026-09-02), not the 27th created.
glama.ai/mcp/servers/theluckystrike/mcp-servers is itself 404, so the canonical repo did not win either.
hypotheses.action: Testable by publishing ONE registry entry whose repository.url names the mirror repo instead of the monorepo. Needs the servers/*/server.json owner plus a registry publish; out of this agent's scope.

hypotheses.claim: Build failure withholds distribution. The Dockerfile in every mirror is the monorepo's and cannot build in the mirror's own context.
for: Measured: docker build on a clone of mcp-invoice fails at 'COPY packages ./packages' with '"/packages": not found'. The mirror has no packages/ or servers/ directory.
glama.ai/mcp/methodology 1.3: a failed build means the profile page is preserved but distribution is withheld.
against: mcp-statement-of-account ships the SAME broken Dockerfile and is listed, scored and returned by the author search, so Glama's AI-inferred Dockerfile succeeded there.
Withheld distribution would mean absent from search, not a 404 on the page.
hypotheses.action: Fix the Dockerfile emitted into mirrors. Owned by whoever owns scripts/sync-mirrors.sh. Round 1 wrongly counted 'Dockerfile serves HTTP 200' as a positive signal; serving is not building.

hypotheses.claim: The official MCP registry drives /mcp/servers listings.
against: bln-mcp-grammar-server is listed at /mcp/servers and is NOT in the official registry (searched registry.modelcontextprotocol.io for 'grammar': 4 results, all io.github.CSOAI-ORG/grammar-fix-ai-mcp).
All 33 mirrors ARE in the registry and 32 have no server page.
hypotheses.action: The registry drives /mcp/connectors only. That is still valuable, see below.

hypotheses.claim: Repo metadata: a topic, a release, a description, a homepage, stars, size or README shape.
against: See the discrimination table: every field is identical or non-discriminating.
hypotheses.action: Do not spend another loop on repo cosmetics for Glama.

hypotheses.claim: Fetching an unindexed page puts it in the queue.
hypotheses.verdict: FALSIFIED in a prior round, not retested per brief

tests_run.test: GitHub traffic referrers, the check the brief expected to settle it
tests_run.result: [] for all five, including the indexed one
tests_run.conclusion: Does not settle it. glama.ai is not a referrer on any repo, because a crawler clones or fetches raw files rather than browsing with a Referer header. Clone counts do not discriminate either. Recorded so no future loop re-spends these calls.

tests_run.test: Docker build of a mirror repo in its own context
tests_run.result: FAILS: 'failed to compute cache key: "/packages": not found' at Dockerfile line 6, COPY packages ./packages
tests_run.conclusion: Every mirror ships the monorepo's Dockerfile, which references packages/ and servers/ directories that do not exist in the mirror. A real defect, but not the cause of the 404s, since the indexed repo has the same file.

tests_run.test: Is a 200 from the badge endpoint proof of a listing?
tests_run.result: definitely-not-a-real-repo-xyz123 -> HTTP 200, 2880 bytes. mcp-change-order -> HTTP 200, 2880 bytes, BYTE-IDENTICAL. mcp-statement-of-account -> HTTP 200, 4558 bytes. Pages: mcp-change-order HEAD 404, mcp-statement-of-account HEAD 200.
tests_run.conclusion: The badge route serves a placeholder SVG for repositories that do not exist. The inherited watch script used badge-200 as its listing test and therefore reported 3 of 33 indexed; the truth is 1 of 33. Pasting such a badge into awesome-mcp-servers would have published a badge for a server that 404s. Fixed: the script now probes the PAGE and fingerprints the placeholder.

tests_run.test: Is the documented daily sync real for an unclaimed server?
tests_run.command: node scripts/glama-watch.mjs; observed_at parsed from the embedded record on the server overview page
tests_run.result: mcp-statement-of-account observed_at = 2026-09-05T18:06:49.992918Z, releaseVersion 0.14.0, claimed=false. Unchanged across releases v0.15.0 through v0.21.0 and the 2026-09-06T08:22 force-push. Every connector was scored 2026-09-08.
tests_run.conclusion: Glama's score page says 'Servers are automatically synced at least once per day'. For this unclaimed server the tool schemas have not been re-read in 4 days and still report v0.14.0 while the project is at v0.21.0. The connector surface re-scores about daily. Falsifiable prediction for loop 32: if observed_at is still 2026-09-05 after the tool descriptions change, the /mcp/servers record cannot measure this work and only connectors can.

discovery_vs_sync.caveat: The punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers CI check matches the literal string 'glama.ai/mcp/servers/', so a connector URL does not satisfy it.

crawler_visit_evidence.referrers: empty on every repo including the indexed one; glama.ai has never appeared as a GitHub traffic referrer
crawler_visit_evidence.clones: all mirrors are cloned heavily (68-325 in 14 days) but the indexed repo is not an outlier, so clones cannot identify Glama
crawler_visit_evidence.positive_proof_of_a_visit: Glama observed 8 tools on mcp-statement-of-account at 2026-09-05T18:06:49.992918Z and recorded a toolSchemaChangelog entry '8 tool updates v0.14.0'. That requires a clone, a build and a live tools/list, so the crawler demonstrably did visit and run that one repo.

single_biggest_lever.why: It is the MINIMUM-scoring tool on 20 of 20 connectors, and 40 percent of the definition-quality score is the minimum tool score. The package is vendored into every server, so one description caps the whole fleet.
single_biggest_lever.current_description: Activate a Pro license key (format MCPL1.xxx.yyy). Verified offline and saved locally.
single_biggest_lever.worst_dimensions_observed: Usage Guidelines 1/5, Purpose 2/5, Behavior 2/5, Completeness 2/5, Conciseness 2/5

modelled_if_lifted_to_3_5.caveat: A model, not a measurement. It assumes only the license tool score changes and coherence is unchanged. The claim must still describe what the tool actually does.

single_biggest_lever.owner: the tool-description agent (servers/*/src and packages/); NOT this agent

connector_health_401.round_1: all 4 connectors rendered a red dot, 'Server is not responding', because https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/<name> returned HTTP 401
connector_health_401.now: FIXED. mcp.zovo.one/mcp/{spreadsheet,statement-of-account,asset-register} all return HTTP 200, and every connector dot in the listing is green #12b981 with zero 'not responding' strings.

rejected_levers.lever: Report tool usage to Glama's unauthenticated telemetry endpoint to clear the 'No recent usage' checklist item
rejected_levers.rejected_because: The usage did not happen. Reporting it would be fabrication, and the checklist item is a claim about real adoption.

rejected_levers.lever: Add mcp-statement-of-account as a fifth entry to awesome-mcp-servers PR 13473 to flip the label
rejected_levers.rejected_because: Already rejected in round 1 and still correct: it would green a gate while four of five entries stay unbadged.

rejected_levers.lever: Delete and recreate the 32 repos to bait the creation-time crawler
rejected_levers.rejected_because: Destructive, and the 120-day lag on bln-mcp-grammar-server shows creation time is not the trigger anyway.

rejected_levers.lever: Create a Glama account to use the documented Add Server flow
rejected_levers.rejected_because: Forbidden by the brief and by standing project rules. Recorded in HUMAN_GATED_PACK.md as an operator click.

recommendations.action: Rewrite the license_activate description in packages/mcp-license/src/index.ts:214-216. It is the fleet minimum on 20 of 20 connectors and 40 percent of the score is the minimum. Nothing else in reach moves as many servers with one edit.
recommendations.measurable_in: about 1 day on the connector surface

recommendations.action: Retarget Glama effort from /mcp/servers to /mcp/connectors. The registry path needs no account, already carries 25 of our servers, carries the identical TDQS, and re-scores daily. /mcp/servers is not enterable autonomously.
The Dockerfile copied into every mirror repo is the monorepo's and cannot build there (measured). Emit a mirror-local Dockerfile, or omit it and let Glama infer one.

Test H2 on ONE server: publish a registry entry whose repository.url names the mirror repo rather than the monorepo, and watch whether a /mcp/servers record appears. This is the only remaining no-account experiment that could open the server surface.
Never treat a 200 from the badge URL as proof of a listing. Check the page, or read badges[<repo>].safe_to_publish in data/glama_watch.json.

budget.note: All Glama requests were paced; the documented limit is 100 requests per second and this stayed near 1.
